name: a-new-tab-lands-at-the-top-of-the-list
description:
A new tab used to be appended, so the newest row sat at the bottom of the space's tab list and the user had to look for it. mutate::open_tab now resolves the first rendered slot instead of the Chromium strip index.

An empty new tab carries no URL and so persists no row. The scenario opens one and loads a page the space does not already hold, which is the first moment a row exists, then reads the order.

actions.expression: (() => { const pane = document.querySelector('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane)'); const rows = [...pane.querySelectorAll('[data-dropzone="tabs"] .tabrow')]; return rows.map((r) => r.querySelector('.tl').textContent).join('|'); })()

(() => { const pane = document.querySelector('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane)'); const b = pane.querySelector('.newtab'); if (!b) { return 'no button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, view: window})); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: dispatched on the button rather than aimed by coordinate - row heights move under other tasks and a pixel click retargets silently.
a page this space does not hold. A URL it already holds would be adopted by that cold row, and no row would be added at all.

actions.expression: (() => { const pane = document.querySelector('.railpane:not(.ovrailpane)'); const rows = [...pane.querySelectorAll('[data-dropzone="tabs"] .tabrow')]; if (rows.length !== 4) { return 'rows ' + rows.length; } const tail = rows.slice(1).map((r) => r.querySelector('.tl').textContent).join('|'); return tail === 'Example Domain|Row Two|Row Three' ? 'new on top' : 'order ' + tail; })()
actions.note: THE GATE. 'rows 3' means the page never opened a row. An 'order ...' answer names where the three older rows ended up, which is what a regression to appending looks like.

assertions.desc: the fixture order as it renders, so the comparison after the load means something
THE MEASUREMENT: the new row is first and the three older rows keep their order below it
